title: Fractional Hall Conductance of Laughlin States from a Topological Index
authors: Sven Bachmann, Severin Schraven, Jacob Shapiro, Simone Warzel
abstract: We provide a rigorous Laughlin-pump argument that establishes the fractional quantization of the Hall conductance directly from the Laughlin state as a topological index. Our proof uses a recently defined index of a pair of pure states together with an infinite matrix product state analysis that is rigorous on a sufficiently thin cylinder. By virtue of the connection to an index, our result implies, in particular, that Laughlin states are representatives of topologically stable fractional quantum Hall phases.
summary: This paper rigorously proves the fractional quantization of the Hall conductance for Laughlin states by defining and calculating a many-body topological index. Using an infinite Matrix Product State formalism on a thin cylinder, the authors show that this index yields $\sigma_H = 1/q$, establishing the quantization as a fundamental topological property of the FQH phase.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously establish the fractional quantization of the Hall conductance ($\sigma_H$) for Laughlin states by deriving it directly from a topological index, bypassing reliance on spectral gap assumptions.
main_result: The authors prove that the Hall conductance for Laughlin states is quantized to $\sigma_H = 1/q$, where $q$ is an integer, demonstrating that this value is a robust topological invariant.
method: The core method involves recasting the Laughlin-pump argument into a topological invariant defined as an index ($	ext{ind}(\omega_1, \omega_2)$) for a pair of pure states, which is then calculated using an infinite Matrix Product State (iMPS) representation.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Fractional Quantum Hall (FQH) effect, modeled by Laughlin states ($\omega_q$). The analysis is performed on a thin cylinder geometry using the CAR algebra of observables.
key_observables: Hall conductance ($\sigma_H$), the topological index ($	ext{ind}(\omega_1, \omega_2)$), and the filling fraction ($1/q$).
important_parameters: The analysis is most rigorous in the thin-cylinder limit (large $\gamma$) and involves the flux quantum insertion parameter $k$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the validity of the iMPS representation for sufficiently large cylinder radii ($\gamma$) and the definition of the index's stability under deformations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the conformal equivalence between a cylinder and an annulus. Figure 2 shows the iMPS representation, detailing how elementary 'squeezing' operations map the root partition related to flux insertion.
paper_structure: The argument progresses by first defining the physical problem (flux insertion $ightarrow \sigma_H$), then abstracting it into a topological index, proving the index's mathematical robustness (automorphism invariance, stability), and finally applying this index to the specific Laughlin state to derive the quantization result.
why_interesting: The use of topological invariants derived from algebraic structures (like the index on the CAR algebra) to prove fundamental quantization results in strongly correlated electron systems provides a powerful, non-perturbative theoretical tool applicable to other quantum many-body problems.
